title: Decode One Instruction: TEST r/m64, r64 (2026-09-24)
blurb:
Decode this 3-byte sequence into a full x86-64 instruction (name it, and state every operand):

48 85 D8

--- Answer ---

`test rax, rbx`

`48` is REX.W (W=1, no register-extension bits), setting 64-bit operand size. `85` is the opcode for TEST r/m64, r64: TEST computes a bitwise AND of its two operands purely to set flags (ZF, SF, PF), discarding the result. The ModRM byte D8 = 11 011 000: mod=11 selects register-direct addressing, reg=011 is rbx, rm=000 is rax, giving test rax, rbx. This idiom is almost always followed by jz/jnz to test whether the two registers are bitwise-disjoint, without needing a spare register for the result.
